vo_face_oval_full_perimeter.evidence: Thumbnail review: loose dark hair overlaps both temples and portions of the lateral jawlines, so the complete skin perimeter cannot be separated cleanly from hair from hairline to chin. Partial visibility is treated as fail.

vo_face_oval_vertical_relation.evidence: Thumbnail and native review: the visible skin face from hairline to chin is moderately longer than its cheek width, without compact roundness or distinctly long parallel sides.

vo_face_oval_width_hierarchy.evidence: Thumbnail and native review: the visible cheekbone line is subtly the widest skin span, while the upper forehead and lower jaw narrow modestly.

vo_face_oval_lower_taper.evidence: Native review: each lower cheek flows through a smooth non-angular jaw taper to a narrow softly rounded chin, with neither a broad corner nor an isolated point.

vo_face_oval_confound_control.evidence: Native review: expression and perspective are restrained, but loose hair overlays the temporal and lateral jaw boundaries; hairstyle can therefore create or conceal part of the apparent oval. Partial control is treated as fail.

supplemental_observations.scene: The saved pixels show one adult botanist holding a transparent orchid evidence panel in a moonlit conservatory with numbered dishes and camera equipment.
supplemental_observations.reference_boundary: The review compares visible appearance only and makes no same-person or biometric identity claim.
